summary: Async bulk job created_at and updated_at values were sourced from raw time() instead of the AIPS_DateTime abstraction required by the coding conventions.
why_it_matters: Bulk job rows store BIGINT Unix timestamps that are read back through AIPS_DateTime::fromTimestamp(). Writing them with raw time() bypasses the single date/time entry point and leaves the persistence path inconsistent with the rest of the plugin.
suggested_fix: Route every lifecycle timestamp write and the cleanup cutoff through AIPS_DateTime::now()->timestamp().
resolution: Replaced all six raw time() call sites (create, mark_completed, mark_processing, update_status, increment_processed, cleanup_old_jobs) with direct AIPS_DateTime::now()->timestamp() calls, matching the convention used elsewhere in the codebase. Behaviour is unchanged: both return the current UTC Unix timestamp.
